title: Coefficientwise extension along an injective ring homomorphism is an injective ring homomorphism
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring homomorphism of commutative rings and $T$ an indeterminate, with polynomial rings $R[T]$ and $S[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The coefficientwise extension along $\varphi$ is the map

$$
\varphi_*:R[T]\longrightarrow S[T],\qquad
\sum_{r\geq0}c_rT^r\longmapsto\sum_{r\geq0}\varphi(c_r)T^r .
$$

It is a ring homomorphism: $\varphi_*(1)=1$, $\varphi_*(P+Q)=\varphi_*(P)+\varphi_*(Q)$, $\varphi_*(PQ)=\varphi_*(P)\varphi_*(Q)$, hence $\varphi_*\bigl(\prod_{j\in J}P_j\bigr)=\prod_{j\in J}\varphi_*(P_j)$ for every finite family $(P_j)_{j\in J}$ in $R[T]$. If $\varphi$ is injective, then $\varphi_*$ is injective: two polynomials with the same image have the same coefficients.

In particular: for a prime $\ell$, the coefficientwise extension $P\mapsto P^{(\ell)}$ from $\mathbf Z[T]$ to $\Ql[T]$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension] is $\varphi_*$ for $\varphi:\mathbf Z\to\Ql$, $c\mapsto c\cdot1_{\Ql}$, so it is a ring homomorphism, injective whenever $\mathbf Z\to\Ql$ is; and for a subfield $K\subset L$ the inclusion $K[T]\subset L[T]$ is $\varphi_*$ for the (injective) inclusion $\varphi:K\hookrightarrow L$, hence injective.
